intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic dishes like Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Stay in a hostel within the Old Quarter itself to maximize time and minimize transit. Since the flight arrives late on Day 1, this tour is best scheduled from Day 2 morning, allowing a full and energetic start to the trip.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Street Food Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An during the monthly Lantern Festival, sampling White Rose Dumplings, Cao Lau noodles, and Banh Mi from street stalls. Book budget guesthouses directly on Tran Phu or Nguyen Thai Hoc streets to stay within walking distance of all activity hubs, avoiding costly and time-consuming transport.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Royal Tomb Bicycle Tour
experiences.description: Rent a bicycle and self-guide through the Imperial Citadel, Thien Mu Pagoda, and the royal tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty along the Perfume River. Stay at a budget hostel near Pham Ngu Lao Street in Hue to be centrally located. This full-day cultural immersion is ideal for backpackers and fits comfortably within a tight budget.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City War Remnants Museum & Ben Thanh Market
experiences.description: Visit the powerful War Remnants Museum in District 3 to understand Vietnam's modern history, then head to Ben Thanh Market for affordable street food including Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes) and fresh spring rolls. Choose a hostel in District 1 or District 3 to stay within a 10-minute walk of both sites, making the most of every day without wasting time on transit.

experiences.name: Ninh Binh Boat Tour through Tam Coc Rice Paddies
experiences.description: Take a scenic 2-hour rowboat ride through the limestone karst caves and emerald rice paddies of Tam Coc, often called 'Halong Bay on land.' Easily reachable by budget bus or motorbike from Hanoi as a day trip or overnight stay. Book accommodation in Ninh Binh town center to be close to boat departure points and local eateries serving Goat Meat — the region's specialty.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the 86 airport bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk around Hoan Kiem Lake (free). Admire the Turtle Tower and snap photos of the iconic red Huc Bridge leading to Ngoc Son Temple.
day_by_day.evening: Dive straight into Old Quarter street food culture. Wander the 36 ancient streets of the Old Quarter, soaking up the chaotic energy, motorbikes, and lantern-lit alleyways. Join the weekend night market on Hang Dao Street if applicable.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Banh Mi from a street cart near the airport or Old Quarter (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a local sidewalk stall on Hang Manh or Ly Quoc Su Street (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a bank in the Old Quarter (avoid hotel exchange rates). Get a local SIM card at the airport (Viettel or Vietnamobile, ~100,000 VND for data). Keep your valuables close in the busy Old Quarter.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the morning exercise scene — locals do tai chi, badminton, and jogging. Visit Ngoc Son Temple (~30,000 VND entry). Then walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral for a look at the French colonial Gothic architecture (free exterior).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND) — one of the best museums in Southeast Asia showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Take a local bus (No. 14, ~9,000 VND) to get there. Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor and outdoor exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter and explore Bia Hoi Corner (corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen streets) — the famous intersection where fresh draft beer costs as little as 5,000–10,000 VND per glass. Mingle with backpackers and locals.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at a local pho shop near the hotel (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle bowl) from a street stall near the museum (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Nem Cuon (fresh spring rolls) and grilled skewers from street vendors at Bia Hoi Corner (~60,000–80,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Bargain politely at any market stalls. The Museum of Ethnology is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (free, but check opening hours — closed Mon & Fri mornings). See the Presidential Palace grounds, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda (~free–15,000 VND). Dress modestly and expect queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first university, built in 1070. Entry ~30,000 VND. Spend 1.5 hours exploring the beautiful courtyards and stelae. Then stroll through Ba Dinh Square nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the Thang Long Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Theatre near Hoan Kiem Lake (~100,000 VND for budget seats) — a uniquely Vietnamese art form. Book tickets in advance at the box office.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street cart (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Rieu (crab and tomato noodle soup) from a local lunch spot near Ba Dinh (~45,000–55,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com Binh Dan (Vietnamese set meal with rice and multiple dishes) at a local canteen-style restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Mausoleum has a strict dress code — no shorts, bare shoulders, or hats inside. Photography is restricted near the mausoleum. Water puppet show lasts about 50 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or open-tour bus from Hanoi to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~80,000–120,000 VND). Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) upon arrival and cycle to Tam Coc. Board a rowboat through the stunning limestone karst caves of Tam Coc (~150,000 VND, ~2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free), a beautiful cave pagoda carved into a limestone cliff. Then bike to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (~20,000 VND) to see the ancient temples of the Dinh and Le dynasties amid dramatic scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus. Rest and recover at the hotel. Take a calm evening walk along Hoan Kiem Lake lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab banh mi or a quick bite near the bus station before departure (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or Bun Cha at a local Ninh Binh eatery near Tam Coc (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pho or simple noodle soup from a sidewalk stall in the Old Quarter upon return (~45,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Start as early as possible (6:30–7:00 AM) to avoid midday heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Watch out for boat ladies trying to sell you goods mid-river — politely decline if not interested. The day trip is long but very rewarding.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hanoi accommodation. Take the Reunification Express train or a budget open-tour bus from Hanoi to Hue (~13–14 hours by train, overnight option, or ~12 hours by bus). Book a sleeper train (hard sleeper ~250,000–350,000 VND) or overnight bus (~200,000–250,000 VND) for budget savings. If taking a daytime train, enjoy the scenic coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: If on a daytime bus or train, enjoy the Vietnamese countryside rolling by. Pack snacks and a book. The train passes through beautiful mountain and coastal scenery around the Hai Van Pass.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hue in the evening (if overnight bus/train, arrive early next morning). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Hue's backpacker area (~150,000–200,000 VND/night). Walk along the Perfume River at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a local Old Quarter spot before departure (~35,000–45,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Snacks, instant noodles, or food from train/bus station vendors (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant upon arrival (~50,000–65,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book transport at least 1–2 days in advance. The overnight sleeper bus is the most budget-friendly option. Secure your belongings on overnight transport. Hue is famous for its royal cuisine — start exploring the local food scene right away.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Dai Noi) — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty (~200,000 VND entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the vast walled complex, the Forbidden Purple City, and beautifully restored pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and ride along the Perfume River to visit the Thien Mu Pagoda (free) — Hue's iconic 7-story pagoda. Continue to the tomb of Emperor Tu Duc (~100,000 VND) set in a serene forested landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll Pham Ngu Lao Street (Hue's backpacker hub) and browse the Dong Ba Market for local snacks and souvenirs. Enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere along the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Hue or Chao (rice porridge) from a morning street stall (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Hen (rice with baby clams) — a Hue specialty from a local market stall (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancake with shrimp and pork) at a local restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hue is very walkable and bikeable. The Imperial City is large — wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Many royal tombs are spread out, so a bicycle or motorbike is ideal. Hue cuisine is spicier than northern Vietnamese food.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or shared minivan from Hue to Hoi An (~3–4 hours, ~120,000–200,000 VND). The route crosses the breathtaking Hai Van Pass — try to sit on the right side for ocean views. Some buses stop at the pass for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An and check in to a budget hostel (~150,000–250,000 VND/night). Walk into the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town (free to enter, ticket needed for heritage sites ~120,000 VND for 5 sites). Explore the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, Chinese Assembly Halls, and ancient merchant houses.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the Ancient Town as it transforms with hundreds of colorful silk lanterns lit at night. Release a paper lantern on the Thu Bon River (~20,000–30,000 VND). Browse the night market on Nguyen Hoang Street.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite before departure or eat at the bus station (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and greens) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~55,000–75,000 VND)
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and grilled skewers from street stalls in the night market (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is extremely popular — book accommodation in advance. The Ancient Town is best explored on foot. Lantern Festival occurs on the 14th of each lunar month when vehicles are banned and lanterns fill the streets — magical if timing aligns. Tailor shops are everywhere; custom clothes are affordable but allow 24–48 hours for fitting.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) and cycle 5 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach — beautiful and less crowded than Da Nang. Swim, relax, and enjoy the coastal scenery. Beach entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle back through rice paddies and visit the Tra Que Vegetable Village (~50,000 VND entry + optional cooking class ~200,000–300,000 VND). Join a short cooking demonstration or simply walk through the organic herb gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An Ancient Town for sunset. Visit the rooftop of a cafe overlooking the river for a cheap local beer or Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da). Explore the local market and practice bargaining for handmade goods.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — Hoi An's most famous banh mi shop (~30,000–45,000 VND). Expect a short queue — worth it!
meals.lunch: Seafood grilled skewers and fresh coconut at a beach shack (~80,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with shrimp and pork) at a local eatery (~50,000–65,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: An Bang Beach has free public access areas. Avoid renting beach chairs/umbrellas from restaurants unless you plan to eat there (often mandatory purchase). Cycling in Hoi An is a joy — roads are flat and scenic. Stay hydrated in the heat.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - 2027-04-23 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City / Saigon)
day_by_day.morning: Check out and take a bus or grab a taxi to Da Nang Airport (~30 min, ~150,000–200,000 VND by taxi or ~20,000 VND by local bus). Fly from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (budget airlines: VietJet, Bamboo — book in advance for ~400,000–800,000 VND). Alternatively, take an overnight sleeper bus (~200,000–300,000 VND, ~15 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Take the 109 airport bus to the city center (~20,000 VND). Check in to a budget hostel in District 1 or Pham Ngu Lao backpacker area (~150,000–250,000 VND/night). Freshen up and head out to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Nguyen Hue Walking Street — a vibrant pedestrian boulevard in the heart of Saigon. Visit the historic City Hall (exterior), the Central Post Office (free to enter, beautiful French colonial interior), and Notre-Dame Cathedral (exterior). End the evening with street food and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hostel or grab a Banh Mi before heading to the airport (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Snacks at the airport or on the plane (budget airlines charge for food — bring your own)
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (Vietnamese sizzling crepe) at a local restaurant in District 1 (~70,000–90,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book flights in advance for the best budget prices. Da Nang airport is small and manageable. In HCMC, beware of motorbike bag snatching — keep bags on the side away from traffic. Grab or Be apps are the safest and cheapest way to get around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — one of the most powerful and moving museums in Vietnam, documenting the Vietnam War through photographs and artifacts. Allow 2 hours. Then walk to Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, frozen in 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ben Thanh Market — browse local goods, street food stalls, and souvenirs. Practice your bargaining skills. Walk through the surrounding streets of District 1 to see the blend of French colonial and modern Vietnamese architecture. Visit the vibrant Bui Vien Walking Street area in the afternoon before it gets too crowded.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — head to Bui Vien Street (the backpacker hub of Saigon) for a lively farewell atmosphere with cheap beers, live music, and street food. Reflect on 10 incredible days of Vietnamese culture, food, and adventure.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Cambodian-style clear pork noodle soup) from a local morning stall (~45,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork chop) — Saigon's iconic dish at a local com tam restaurant (~55,000–75,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food feast on Bui Vien: grilled corn, fresh spring rolls, skewers, and cold Saigon beer (~100,000–150,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — take your time and be respectful. Ben Thanh Market is touristy but fun for a final souvenir shop — bargain hard (start at 50% of asking price). Keep some VND for last-minute street food and transport to the airport. Enjoy your final Vietnamese meal — the food alone is worth coming back for!

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a taxi or airport bus (Bus 86) to the Old Quarter hotel. Check-in, freshen up, and get oriented with a short walk around the immediate neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Old Quarter on foot — wander the 36 ancient streets, browse local shops selling silk, lacquerware, and handicrafts. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the iconic red Huc Bridge leading to Ngoc Son Temple (small entrance fee ~20,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday–Sunday) or explore the buzzing Ta Hien Street 'Beer Corner' for a cold Bia Hoi (draft beer for ~5,000 VND). Soak in the lively Old Quarter atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (the famous Obama-Bourdain spot) — try the classic bun cha with grilled pork and vermicelli noodles (~60,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Banh Mi 25 on Hang Ca Street for a fresh Vietnamese baguette sandwich (~35,000 VND), followed by Egg Coffee at Cafe Giang (~25,000 VND) — a Hanoi institution.

day_by_day.notes: Keep the first afternoon light due to travel fatigue. Exchange currency at a local gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates than the airport. Grab a local SIM card at the airport for data.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (open mornings, closed Mon & Fri) — see the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Arrive early (~8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Entrance is free but dress respectfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entrance) — one of Southeast Asia's best museums showcasing 54 ethnic minority groups through artifacts, clothing, and outdoor traditional houses. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the famous Pho experience. Walk along Hang Bong and Hang Gai streets for evening shopping. End the night with a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Theatre (~100,000 VND) — a uniquely Vietnamese art form.

meals.breakfast: Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street — legendary pho bo (beef noodle soup) since 1955, opens at 6 AM (~50,000 VND). Expect a queue but it moves fast.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near the Ethnology Museum — banh cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a local stall (~40,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — Hanoi's signature turmeric-marinated fish dish with dill and peanuts (~150,000–200,000 VND per person). A cultural dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and for about 2 months annually (Sept–Nov) for maintenance — check ahead. Wear long sleeves and no shorts at the mausoleum.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh — book a budget bus or join a shared tour (~200,000–300,000 VND round trip, ~2 hrs). Visit Trang An Grottoes — a UNESCO World Heritage landscape of limestone karsts and river caves. Rent a rowboat (~200,000 VND per boat, fits 2–3 people) for a 2-hour scenic cave tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or rent a motorbike (~100,000 VND/day) to Bich Dong Pagoda (free entry) and the ancient capital of Hoa Lu (~20,000 VND). Explore the 10th-century royal temples surrounded by dramatic karst scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by early evening. Relax and enjoy a leisurely dinner in the Old Quarter. Visit a rooftop bar for evening drinks with views over the city.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or grab xoi (sticky rice) from a street vendor near the hotel (~20,000 VND) before departing.
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Ninh Binh — try com chay (crispy rice with pork and mushrooms), a Ninh Binh specialty (~80,000–120,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) at a local Old Quarter restaurant (~70,000 VND). Refreshing after a day of sightseeing.

day_by_day.notes: Start early (depart by 7:30 AM) to maximize time in Ninh Binh. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and light rain gear as weather can be unpredictable. Ninh Binh is easily done as a day trip from Hanoi.

day_by_day.morning: Take an overnight sleeper bus or morning train to Hue (~14 hrs by train or book a budget flight for ~500,000–800,000 VND). If flying, depart morning and arrive midday. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Hue's city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Hue Royal Citadel) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors (~150,000 VND entrance). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City, ornate gates, and royal gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River embankment at sunset — a beautiful and peaceful setting. Explore Dong Ba Market for local souvenirs and street food. Join locals for an evening stroll along the riverbank.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the train/bus or at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Upon arrival in Hue — try Banh Mi Phuong (or a local equivalent) or com hen (rice with baby mussels), a Hue street food specialty (~40,000–60,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Hanh Restaurant — a beloved local spot for authentic Hue royal cuisine. Try bun bo Hue (spicy lemongrass beef noodle soup) and nem lui (grilled pork skewers) (~100,000–150,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: Budget flights from Hanoi to Hue (Phu Bai Airport) are the fastest option. Book in advance for best prices. Alternatively, the train offers a scenic overnight journey — book a soft sleeper berth for comfort (~300,000–500,000 VND).

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~100,000–150,000 VND/day) and follow the Royal Tombs route south of Hue. Visit the elaborate Tomb of Khai Dinh (~150,000 VND) — a striking fusion of Vietnamese and European architecture — and the serene Tomb of Tu Duc (~150,000 VND) set among pine forests and lotus ponds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda — Hue's most iconic pagoda on the banks of the Perfume River (free entry). Then take a dragon boat cruise on the Perfume River (~150,000–200,000 VND per person) back toward the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Pham Ngu Lao Street area for backpacker-friendly bars and restaurants. Enjoy a traditional Hue royal dinner performance (optional, ~300,000 VND) or keep it casual with street food.

meals.breakfast: Banh beo (steamed rice cakes with shrimp) from a local street stall near the guesthouse (~30,000–40,000 VND) — a quintessential Hue breakfast.
meals.lunch: Street food near the tombs — banh khoai (Hue sizzling pancake with shrimp and pork) (~50,000–70,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Lac Thien Restaurant — famous for its deaf-mute family service and delicious banh khoai and nem lui (~100,000–130,000 VND per person). A unique cultural dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Hue is best explored by bicycle or motorbike — the city is relatively flat and distances between sights are manageable. Bring water and sun protection for the tomb visits which have limited shade.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Hue to Hoi An via the scenic Hai Van Pass — hire a motorbike taxi (xe om) or join a group tour on the Hai Van Pass (~300,000–500,000 VND). Stop at the summit for panoramic views of Da Nang Bay. Alternatively, take a bus (~100,000 VND, ~3 hrs) via Da Nang.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An and check into a mid-range guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Cau Chua Pagoda), the Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and wander the lantern-lit streets.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hoi An at its magical best — the Ancient Town glows with hundreds of colorful silk lanterns after dark. Buy a lantern (~20,000 VND) and release it on the Thu Bon River. Browse the night market for handicrafts and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the guesthouse in Hue or grab food before departure.
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) at White Rose Restaurant — a Hoi An specialty you can only get here (~80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Cao Lau — Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and local greens, available only in Hoi An due to its unique local well water (~60,000–80,000 VND). Try it at Thanh Cao Lau street stall.

day_by_day.notes: The Ancient Town charges an entrance fee (~120,000 VND) that includes access to 5 heritage sites. The Hai Van Pass route is one of the most scenic drives in Vietnam — highly recommended on a clear day. Check weather before deciding on transport.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (~5 km from town) for a relaxing morning swim. The ride through rice paddies and local villages is scenic and enjoyable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and join a half-day Vietnamese cooking class (~400,000–600,000 VND) — learn to make local dishes like banh xeo (sizzling pancakes), fresh spring rolls, and cao lau. Most classes include a market tour.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the tailors and lantern shops of the Ancient Town — Hoi An is famous for custom-made clothing (24–48 hr turnaround). Place any tailoring orders tonight. Enjoy a sunset drink at one of the riverside bars along Bach Dang Street.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — arguably Vietnam's most famous banh mi shop, beloved by Anthony Bourdain (~30,000–40,000 VND). Arrive early as queues form quickly.
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class — you eat what you cook!
meals.dinner: Morning Glory Restaurant by chef Trinh Diem Vy — upscale Vietnamese street food in a beautiful Ancient Town setting (~150,000–250,000 VND per person). A mid-range splurge worth it.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance — popular classes fill up quickly. If you ordered tailored clothes, pick them up before leaving Hoi An. An Bang Beach is less crowded than Cua Dai and has better beach bars.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or budget flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — flights take ~1 hr (~500,000–900,000 VND). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district or District 1. Drop bags and head out to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a powerful and sobering collection of photographs and artifacts from the Vietnam War. Then walk to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, frozen in time since 1975.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Ben Thanh Market area for street food and local shopping. Walk along Nguyen Hue Walking Street — HCMC's pedestrian boulevard with fountains and the iconic City Hall. Experience the chaotic and exhilarating HCMC evening traffic.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab pho from a street stall in Hoi An before departing.
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa on Le Thi Rieng Street — widely considered the best banh mi in Saigon (~35,000–45,000 VND). Expect a queue.
meals.dinner: Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork vermicelli) from a street stall near Pham Ngu Lao (~50,000 VND), followed by fresh fruit smoothies from a sidewalk vendor (~30,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: HCMC traffic is intense — use Grab (Vietnam's Uber) for convenient and affordable transport (~30,000–80,000 VND per ride). The War Remnants Museum is emotionally heavy — allow time to process. Keep valuables secure in busy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Full day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km from HCMC) — join a half-day tour (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport and entrance). Explore the 250 km network of underground tunnels used by Viet Cong guerrillas during the war. Try crawling through a section of the tunnels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon. Visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu) — a stunning Taoist temple with intricate wooden carvings and incense-filled halls (free entry, donations welcome). Then explore the colorful and vibrant Chinatown (Cho Lon) district.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's famous backpacker street, buzzing with bars, live music, and street food. Experience the electric nightlife atmosphere. Try a Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da) at a sidewalk cafe.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Cambodian-style pork noodle soup) from a local stall near Pham Ngu Lao (~50,000–70,000 VND) — a Saigon breakfast staple.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks at Cu Chi Tunnels site (~50,000–80,000 VND) or eat at a local restaurant near the tunnels.
meals.dinner: Quan Bui Garden Restaurant in District 1 — beautiful garden setting serving modern Vietnamese cuisine (~150,000–250,000 VND per person). A relaxed mid-range dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book Cu Chi Tunnels tour the night before through your guesthouse or a reputable local operator. Wear dark, comfortable clothing as the tunnels are narrow and dirty. The Ben Duoc site is less touristy than Ben Dinh and recommended for a more authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Vietnam — visit the HCMC Museum (~30,000 VND) for a comprehensive overview of the city's history from prehistoric times to the present. Then stroll through the French Quarter — admire the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon (exterior) and the ornate Central Post Office designed by Gustave Eiffel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market or the nearby Saigon Square for better prices. Visit a local cafe for a final Vietnamese iced coffee and reflect on the journey. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with city views. Head to the airport — allow 2–3 hours before departure for international flights. Tan Son Nhat International Airport is ~7 km from District 1 (~80,000–150,000 VND by Grab).

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (fried egg banh mi) from a street cart (~25,000 VND) — a simple and satisfying Saigon breakfast.
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork chop, egg, and pickled vegetables) at Com Tam Thuan Kieu or any local com tam stall (~60,000–80,000 VND) — the quintessential Saigon lunch dish.
meals.dinner: Cuc Gach Quan Restaurant — a charming villa restaurant serving home-style Vietnamese cooking in a rustic antique setting (~200,000–300,000 VND per person). A memorable farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and check-in online if possible. Keep some VND for airport snacks and final tips. Reflect on 10 incredible days — from Hanoi's ancient streets to Saigon's electric energy, Vietnam's diversity of food, culture, and landscapes makes it one of Southeast Asia's most rewarding destinations.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in the Old Quarter. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the labyrinthine streets of the Old Quarter – explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and soak in the colonial architecture and street life at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake (Cà phê Đinh or Skyline Rooftop). Followed by a curated introduction to Hanoi's street food scene with a private food guide – sample Bún Chả, Bánh Mì, and Bia Hơi on Tạ Hiện Street (Beer Street).

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit
meals.dinner: Private street food tour on Tạ Hiện Street followed by a nightcap dinner at Chả Cá Thăng Long – a legendary Hanoi restaurant specializing in the iconic grilled turmeric fish dish, Chả Cá Lã Vọng.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport pickup in advance with your boutique hotel. Confirm a private luxury vehicle (Mercedes or equivalent). Keep Day 1 light – jet lag may be a factor. Exchange some USD to VND at the airport or hotel for street food tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk around Hoan Kiem Lake – watch locals practice Tai Chi and morning exercises. Visit Ngoc Son Temple (Jade Mountain Temple) on the lake island, accessible via the iconic red Huc Bridge. Explore the Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu), Vietnam's first national university, a stunning example of traditional Vietnamese architecture dating to 1070.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology – one of Southeast Asia's finest cultural museums showcasing the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam. Enjoy a private guided tour for deeper cultural context. Return to the Old Quarter for a bespoke cyclo (rickshaw) tour through the 36 ancient guild streets.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thăng Long Water Puppet Theatre – a UNESCO-recognized art form unique to Vietnam. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Phở Bò (beef pho) breakfast at the legendary Phở Thìn on Đinh Tiên Hoàng – a Hanoi institution since 1955.
meals.lunch: Bún Bò Nam Bộ (Southern-style beef noodles) at a well-regarded local eatery near the Museum of Ethnology.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane – a celebrated French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant in a beautifully restored colonial villa, offering a refined tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Water Puppet Show tickets in advance – evening performances sell out quickly. The Museum of Ethnology is best visited on weekday mornings to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – April 17, 2027 (Hanoi to Ha Long Bay)
day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Pack an overnight bag for a 2-night luxury cruise on Ha Long Bay. Private transfer departs the Old Quarter at approximately 08:00 for the 3.5-hour scenic drive to Tuan Chau Marina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board your premium overnight junk cruise (recommended: Indochine Sails, Paradise Elegance, or Orchid Classic). Settle into your private cabin with panoramic bay views. The cruise sets sail through the emerald waters of Ha Long Bay – a UNESCO World Heritage Site with over 1,600 limestone karst islands. Afternoon kayaking through hidden lagoons and sea caves, including the spectacular Luon Cave.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the sundeck as the sky turns golden over the karsts. Cooking demonstration of Vietnamese spring rolls by the onboard chef. Candlelit gourmet seafood dinner on deck featuring fresh squid, prawns, and local fish.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique hotel in Hanoi before departure.
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch served onboard the cruise shortly after boarding – fresh seafood, Vietnamese salads, and spring rolls.
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course seafood dinner onboard the cruise with complimentary wine and cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Pack light for the cruise – a small overnight bag is sufficient. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and swimwear. The cruise includes all meals and most activities. Confirm cruise booking at least 2–3 weeks in advance for premium cabins.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – April 18, 2027 (Ha Long Bay – Bai Tu Long)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the sundeck at sunrise. After breakfast, explore the less-touristed Bai Tu Long Bay by kayak or bamboo boat through hidden caves and floating fishing villages. Visit a pearl farm and learn about the traditional craft of pearl cultivation in Ha Long Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a secluded beach on one of Ha Long's private islands for swimming and relaxation. Optional: squid fishing off the stern of the boat. The cruise begins its return journey toward the marina in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset dinner onboard as the cruise returns. Disembark at Tuan Chau Marina by approximately 18:00. Private luxury transfer back to Hanoi Old Quarter, arriving around 21:30.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast onboard with Vietnamese coffee, fresh tropical fruits, and hot dishes.
meals.lunch: Onboard lunch with a fresh seafood spread and Vietnamese rice dishes.
meals.dinner: Light late dinner upon return to Hanoi – Bánh Cuốn (steamed rice rolls) at a late-night local eatery in the Old Quarter, or room service at the boutique hotel.

day_by_day.notes: The return transfer from Ha Long to Hanoi can be tiring. Consider booking a spa treatment at the hotel for the following morning. Keep the evening of Day 4 flexible and low-key.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19, 2027 (Hanoi – Ninh Binh Day Trip)
day_by_day.morning: Restorative morning – sleep in or enjoy a hotel spa treatment. Late breakfast at the hotel. Depart by private car at 10:00 for Ninh Binh (approximately 2 hours south of Hanoi) – often called 'Ha Long Bay on Land' for its dramatic limestone karst landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ninh Binh and explore the ancient capital of Hoa Lư – Vietnam's first capital, featuring 10th-century royal temples dedicated to Emperor Đinh Tiên Hoàng. Take a traditional sampan boat ride through Tam Cốc ('Three Caves') along the Ngô Đồng River, drifting through rice paddies and towering karsts. Cycle through Trang An Landscape Complex (UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by private car, arriving around 20:00. Relaxed evening in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Late hotel breakfast or Xôi (sticky rice) from a renowned Old Quarter vendor.
meals.lunch: Traditional goat meat (Dê núi) lunch at a local restaurant in Ninh Binh – a regional specialty not to be missed.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca La Vong or The Gioi Nuoc Mam (The World of Fish Sauce) in Hanoi – a premium Vietnamese restaurant celebrating regional flavors.

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring insect repellent. The boat ride at Tam Cốc is approximately 2 hours.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – April 20, 2027 (Fly Hanoi to Hoi An via Da Nang)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Old Quarter boutique hotel. Private transfer to Noi Bai Airport for a morning domestic flight to Da Nang (approximately 1 hour 15 minutes). Upon arrival, private luxury transfer to Hoi An Ancient Town (approximately 30 km, 45 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a premium riverside hotel or boutique resort in Hoi An (recommended: Anantara Hoi An Resort or The Nam Hai). After settling in, explore the UNESCO-listed Hoi An Ancient Town on foot – visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Chùa Cầu), the Phúc Kiến Assembly Hall, and the Old Town merchant houses. Browse the legendary tailor shops on Trần Phú Street for bespoke clothing.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the Ancient Town as it transforms into a magical lantern-lit spectacle after dark. Join a premium Hoi An cooking class at a riverside venue to learn to prepare Cao Lầu, White Rose Dumplings, and Bánh Mì.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before checkout in Hanoi.
meals.lunch: Cao Lầu (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at Trung Bắc Restaurant – a legendary local institution in the Ancient Town.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Morning Glory Restaurant by celebrated chef Triệu Thị Chơi – one of Hoi An's most acclaimed dining destinations, offering refined Central Vietnamese cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Hoi An cooking class in advance. Hoi An Ancient Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. The town is particularly magical during the Lantern Festival (14th day of each lunar month) – check if this coincides with your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise bicycle ride through the lush rice paddies and vegetable gardens surrounding Hoi An with a private guide. Visit Trà Quế Herb Village – a centuries-old organic farming village where you can participate in traditional farming activities and learn about the herbs that define Central Vietnamese cuisine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the My Son Sanctuary – a cluster of ancient Hindu temples built by the Cham Kingdom between the 4th and 14th centuries, a UNESCO World Heritage Site set dramatically in a jungle valley. Private guided tour with an expert archaeologist for deep historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An for a private lantern-making workshop with a local artisan family. Release a lantern on the Thu Bon River at dusk – a deeply moving Hoi An tradition. Dinner at a premium riverside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Bánh Mì Phương – widely considered the world's best Bánh Mì, as endorsed by Anthony Bourdain. A quintessential Hoi An morning ritual.
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Bánh Bao Vac) and Fried Wonton at White Rose Restaurant – the only establishment authorized to make this Hoi An specialty.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Deck House or Mango Mango – premium riverside dining with panoramic Ancient Town views and a sophisticated Vietnamese-fusion menu.

day_by_day.notes: My Son is approximately 40 km from Hoi An (1 hour by private car). Morning visits are recommended to avoid the afternoon heat. Bring comfortable shoes and a hat for the temple complex.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22, 2027 (Da Nang – Marble Mountains & Ba Na Hills)
day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Da Nang (45 minutes). Visit the Marble Mountains (Ngũ Hành Sơn) – a cluster of five marble and limestone hills dotted with Buddhist sanctuaries, caves, and panoramic viewpoints. Climb to the summit of Thủy Sơn for sweeping views of Da Nang's coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cable car ride up to Ba Na Hills – a French colonial hill station perched at 1,487 meters, offering cool mountain air and spectacular views. Explore the fantasy-like French Village, visit the iconic Golden Bridge (held aloft by giant stone hands), and stroll through manicured gardens. Return to Hoi An by private transfer in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Hoi An. Optional: private sunset boat cruise along the Thu Bon River with cocktails and canapés, followed by a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at your Hoi An resort.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ba Na Hills' Le Jardin D'Hiver Restaurant – a charming French-style brasserie with mountain views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vy's Market Restaurant & Cooking School – a vibrant open-air market restaurant in Hoi An celebrating Central Vietnamese street food in an upscale setting.

day_by_day.notes: Ba Na Hills can be crowded on weekends. Arrive early (cable car opens at 07:30) for the best experience. The Golden Bridge is one of Vietnam's most photographed landmarks – ideal for photography in the morning light.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 – April 23, 2027 (Fly to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hoi An – leisurely breakfast at the resort. Last-minute browsing of the Ancient Town's artisan boutiques for bespoke silk items, lacquerware, and handcrafted lanterns. Check out and private transfer to Da Nang Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Domestic flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) – approximately 1 hour 15 minutes. Private luxury transfer to your hotel in District 1 (recommended: Park Hyatt Saigon, The Reverie Saigon, or Capella Hanoi equivalent in HCMC). Check in and explore the vibrant Dong Khoi Street area – the city's elegant colonial boulevard lined with boutiques, galleries, and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Majestic or Caravelle Hotel – iconic Saigon institutions with panoramic Saigon River views. Explore the buzzing Ben Thanh Market area and Bui Vien Walking Street for an electrifying introduction to Ho Chi Minh City's nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Hoi An before checkout.
meals.lunch: Cơm Tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) at a celebrated local restaurant in District 1 upon arrival in HCMC – a quintessential Saigon street food experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nhà Hàng Ngon (Restaurant Ngon) – a stunning colonial villa restaurant in District 1 serving authentic Vietnamese street food dishes from all three regions in an upscale garden setting.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City traffic can be intense – allow extra time for transfers. District 1 is the ideal base for exploring the city's cultural and culinary highlights. Keep valuables secure on busy streets.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 – April 24, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City – Final Day)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reunification Palace (Dinh Thống Nhất) – a powerful symbol of Vietnam's modern history, preserved exactly as it was on April 30, 1975. Explore the War Remnants Museum for a deeply moving and thought-provoking account of the Vietnam War. Visit the Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon and the ornate French Colonial Central Post Office – architectural masterpieces from the French colonial era.
day_by_day.afternoon: Half-day premium excursion to the Cu Chi Tunnels (approximately 70 km northwest of HCMC) – an extraordinary network of underground tunnels used by Viet Cong forces during the war. Private guided tour with a historian. Return to HCMC for a leisurely final afternoon – visit the Bến Thành Market for premium Vietnamese handicrafts, silk, and lacquerware as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a world-class Saigon restaurant. Final evening stroll along the Saigon Riverfront Promenade (Bạch Đằng Wharf) to reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Hủ Tiếu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style noodle soup) – a beloved Saigon breakfast staple at a renowned local eatery in District 5 (Chinatown).
meals.lunch: Bánh Xèo (sizzling Vietnamese crepes) at Bánh Xèo 46A – a legendary HCMC institution.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Quince Saigon or The Social Club Rooftop – a premium rooftop dining experience with panoramic city views, celebrating the finest in contemporary Vietnamese and international cuisine with cocktail pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and arrange private airport transfer in advance. The Cu Chi Tunnels tour takes approximately 4–5 hours including travel. For a deeper experience, book the exclusive 'Veteran's Tour' with a former Cu Chi tunnel fighter as your guide. Leave time for last-minute packing and souvenir shopping before departure.
